ns2:section.sectionText: This course is an in-depth introduction to theories of international trade --- and related empirics. Vis-a-vis international finance or international macro, `international trade' abstracts from monetary aspects and focuses on real international trade flows. The aim is to understand key models and tools in order to interpret the nature of international trade flows and evaluate the effects of trade policy changes on resource allocation, income distribution and aggregate welfare via different channels. It should prepare a student to undertake professional research, and teaching in the field at undergraduate and masters levels.
ns2:section.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Economics department.
